behavior_items: The crate opts into two unstable language features: `auto_traits` and `unboxed_closures`. This means the reproducer is intentionally exercising nightly-only parts of the compiler, especially around trait definitions and the special `Fn` family of callable traits.

The code defines a normal user trait `T` with `trait T {}`. This trait has no implementations in the program, but its name is later used in a function signature position that looks like a callable argument list.
The function `f` is declared as `fn f() -> impl Fn(T)`. This uses return-position `impl Trait`, so the concrete return type is hidden while being required to implement something written as `Fn(T)`.

The syntax `Fn(T)` is significant because, with `unboxed_closures`, the built-in callable traits are written in tuple-style argument form such as `Fn(Args) -> Output`. The reproducer is therefore probing the parser, name resolution, and trait lowering logic for parenthesized callable-trait notation.

Inside `f`, the local `p` is bound to the unit value `()`, and the closure `|_| p` is returned. This closure ignores its single argument and returns the captured local `p`, so semantically it is a one-argument closure with output type `()`.

That closure captures `p` by reference or by value as needed and is expected to implement the standard callable traits for a one-argument closure. In ordinary Rust, such a closure would implement the lang-item `core::ops::FnOnce`, and possibly `FnMut`/`Fn`, with an argument tuple corresponding to one parameter and output `()`.

The reproducer deliberately introduces `auto trait Fn { type Output; }`, defining a user item named `Fn`. This is important because `Fn` is also the name used by Rust’s built-in callable trait machinery. The code is therefore testing what happens when a user-defined trait name collides with the special callable-trait name.

This user-defined `Fn` is declared as an `auto trait`. Auto traits are marker-like traits whose implementations are synthesized automatically by the compiler based on field contents, similar to `Send` and `Sync`. They are highly restricted in Rust.

The declaration `auto trait Fn { type Output; }` is especially provocative because auto traits are not supposed to have associated items such as associated types. By adding `type Output;`, the reproducer forces the compiler to validate restrictions on auto trait contents.

The same declaration also interacts with the special meaning of the identifier `Fn`. The compiler must distinguish between the built-in callable trait syntax/lowering and an ordinary trait item in user code, even when that trait is named `Fn`.

When the compiler processes `fn f() -> impl Fn(T)`, it must resolve whether `Fn` refers to the built-in callable trait family or to the user-defined auto trait named `Fn`. This is a subtle name-resolution and AST/HIR lowering scenario because the callable-trait syntax is special-cased in the language.

If the compiler treats `Fn(T)` as callable-trait notation, then it expects the trait behind it to participate in the `extern "rust-call"` ABI and tupled argument machinery used by the lang-item `Fn` traits. A user-defined auto trait cannot satisfy those expectations, so this path stresses compiler validation.

If instead the compiler resolves `Fn` to the locally declared auto trait, it still has to decide whether the parenthesized `(T)` is legal trait generic syntax or special callable syntax. Since `T` here is a trait name, not a concrete type tuple, this can further stress parsing, type checking, and diagnostics.

The closure `|_| p` returning `()` is compatible with a callable signature taking one argument and producing `()`, but it is not meaningfully related to a custom auto trait with an associated type. This mismatch helps expose whether the compiler incorrectly conflates closure traits with user-defined items named `Fn`.

The reproducer therefore exercises multiple compiler phases together: feature gating for unstable features, parsing of `Fn(...)` syntax, item validation for auto traits, name resolution of `Fn`, lowering of closure signatures, return-position `impl Trait`, and type checking of closure trait implementation.

Lowers a path segment naming a type-like item by first lowering its generic arguments and then either creating a lazy type-alias projection or instantiating the item’s declared type. It calls `tcx` for definition/type queries and calls `lower_generic_args_of_path_segment` to obtain the segment arguments.

Filters the provided trait-bound candidates to those whose trait defines the requested associated item by calling `probe_trait_that_defines_assoc_item`. If none match, it reports the failure via `complain_about_assoc_item_not_found`; if multiple match, it builds an ambiguity diagnostic and may lower constraint types/consts with `lower_ty`; otherwise it returns the single matching `PolyTraitRef`.

Lowers a qualified associated path on `qself_ty` by first probing enum variants with `probe_adt` and rejecting unexpected generics with `prohibit_generic_args`, then trying inherent associated types via `probe_inherent_assoc_ty`. If neither applies, it resolves the defining trait bound using `probe_single_bound_for_assoc_item` or `probe_single_ty_param_bound_for_assoc_item`, and returns the lowered associated item type together with its `DefKind` and `DefId`.

Searches inherent impls of an ADT for an inherent associated type with the given name by calling `probe_assoc_item_unchecked`, then selects the applicable impl with `select_inherent_assoc_type_candidates`. After selection it validates accessibility with `check_assoc_item`, lowers any explicit associated-item generics with `lower_generic_args_of_assoc_item`, and returns the resulting alias type and definition id.

Tests each inherent associated type candidate in an inference context by unifying its impl self type with the requested `self_ty` and checking impl obligations. If no candidate applies it reports the error with `complain_about_inherent_assoc_ty_not_found`; if several apply it reports ambiguity with `complain_about_ambiguous_inherent_assoc_ty`; otherwise it returns the unique applicable candidate.
Looks up an associated item in a scope by first calling `probe_assoc_item_unchecked`, then validating visibility and stability with `check_assoc_item` before returning the found item.

Performs unchecked associated-item lookup in a scope by adjusting the identifier and scope hygienically, then scanning `tcx.associated_items(scope)` for an item of the requested name and kind. Returns both the matched item and the adjusted definition scope.
Checks that an associated item is accessible and stable at the use site. It emits a privacy error when the item is not visible, then always performs stability checking with `tcx.check_stability`.

Collects accessible trait names whose associated types could match the requested associated-type name for `qself_ty`. It filters all traits by associated-type presence, visibility, and existence of a non-negative impl whose self type can unify with `qself_ty`, then returns their path strings.

Lowers a fully qualified associated type path. If the self type is missing it calls `error_missing_qpath_self_ty`; otherwise it lowers the trait reference with `lower_mono_trait_ref`, lowers associated-item generic arguments with `lower_generic_args_of_assoc_item`, and constructs the projection type.

Rejects generic arguments and associated-item constraints on path segments. It reports generic-argument misuse with `report_prohibit_generics_error`, and if constraints are present it reports the first one via `prohibit_assoc_item_constraint`.

Classifies which path segments are allowed to carry generic arguments for a resolved path, based on the resolved item kind and optional self type. It inspects constructors, enum variants, parents, generics, and ADTs to return the list of `GenericPathSegment` positions that should accept generics.

Lowers a resolved HIR path into a type by dispatching on `path.res`. Depending on the case it rejects misplaced generics with `prohibit_generic_args`, lowers path arguments with `lower_generic_args_of_path_segment`, classifies generic-bearing segments with `probe_generic_path_segments`, lowers ordinary segments with `lower_path_segment`, lowers qualified associated paths with `lower_qpath`, and lowers type parameters with `lower_ty_param`; it also emits diagnostics and produces error types for invalid path forms.
Lowers a type parameter reference from name resolution into either a late-bound type, an early-bound param, or an error type, based on `tcx.named_bound_var`.
Lowers a const-parameter reference from name resolution into either an early-bound `ParamConst`, a late-bound const, or an error const, based on `tcx.named_bound_var`.

Main recursive HIR-type lowering entry point. It lowers delegation placeholders with `lower_delegation_ty`, references by calling `lower_lifetime` and `lower_ty`, tuples/slices/pointers recursively via `lower_ty`, bare function types by calling `lower_fn_ty`, trait objects by calling `prohibit_or_lint_bare_trait_object_ty` and `lower_trait_object_ty`, paths by calling `lower_path`, and constructs error types for invalid return-type-notation uses.
Returns the inherited input or output type for a delegation placeholder by reading the delegation signature from `inherit_sig_for_delegation_item`.

Lowers an opaque type reference by building its generic arguments from the opaque item's generics, resolving supplied lifetime arguments with `lower_lifetime`. It returns either a projection type for trait context or an opaque type otherwise.
Lowers a function argument type, but if the HIR uses `_` and an expected type is available it records that type with `record_ty` and reuses it; otherwise it calls `lower_ty`.

Lowers a function type into a `PolyFnSig` by calling `lower_fn_sig`, wrapping the result with late-bound vars, validating CMSE ABI rules, and then checking late-bound lifetime well-formedness with `validate_late_bound_regions`.

When lowering `_` in an impl method signature, tries to recover the corresponding trait method type. It lowers the impl's trait reference with `lower_impl_trait_ref` after lowering the self type with `lower_ty`, finds the matching associated function, and returns either the selected input type or output type from the instantiated trait signature.

Emits errors for late-bound lifetimes referenced in a function return type but not constrained by the inputs. For each such region it constructs a diagnostic with the supplied callback and adds extra notes for anonymous lifetimes before emitting it.

Computes the lifetime bound for a trait object from its existential predicates using `object_region_bounds`. It returns `None` when no derived bound exists, prefers `'static` when present, and otherwise returns the unique derived region while emitting an ambiguity error if multiple distinct bounds are found.

Finds the unique trait bound on a type parameter that defines the requested associated type. It calls `tcx` to access HIR/type context data, `probe_ty_param_bounds` to collect the parameter’s bounds, reads the parameter name from HIR, and then calls `probe_single_bound_for_assoc_item` with candidates produced by `traits::transitive_bounds_that_define_assoc_item`.
Lowers a HIR type specifically in path context by directly calling `lower_ty_common` with `borrowed = false` and `in_path = true`.

Validates that a delegated signature does not use unsupported forms and reports diagnostics when requested. It calls `tcx` repeatedly to inspect spans, local HIR nodes, generics, parent item information, definition kinds, and associated item metadata, and calls `dcx`/`emit_err` through the local `try_emit` closure to report delegation errors.

Core HIR-to-`Ty` lowering dispatcher that converts each `hir::TyKind` into the corresponding internal type form. Depending on the variant, it calls `tcx`, `lower_delegation_ty`, `lower_ty`, `lower_lifetime`, `lower_fn_ty`, `prohibit_or_lint_bare_trait_object_ty`, `lower_trait_object_ty`, `lower_path`, `lower_opaque_ty`, and `require_c_abi_if_c_variadic`, while also using `hir` queries and `associated_type_for_impl_trait_in_trait` for opaque/path-related lowering.
Returns the human-readable string for an associated item kind (`function`, `constant`, or `type`). It does not call any other methods in the provided Methods List.

Emits a `MissingTypeParams` diagnostic when the collected missing type-parameter list is non-empty, using the item definition span and the source snippet for the use site. This method does not call any other method from the provided Methods List.

Reports misuse of internal `Fn`-family trait syntax: it returns early when `unboxed_closures` is enabled, rejects parenthesized syntax on non-`Fn` traits, suggests parenthetical `Fn(A) -> B` notation for stable `Fn` traits when appropriate, and emits a manual-implementation error for impls. This method explicitly calls `fn_trait_to_string` from the Methods List to build the suggested `Fn`-trait spelling.

Builds the main diagnostic for a missing associated item on a type parameter by searching candidate traits, first preferring a more precise kind-mismatch error, then trying typo suggestions, visibility-aware trait suggestions, and finally hints to add trait bounds or use a qualified path. This method explicitly calls `complain_about_assoc_kind_mismatch` from the Methods List when it finds an associated item with the right name but the wrong kind.

Emits an `AssocKindMismatch` diagnostic when an associated type/const/function name exists but was used as the wrong kind, computing targeted labels for bound-vs-equality constraints and an optional brace-wrapping suggestion for associated-const equality syntax. This method does not call any other method from the provided Methods List.

Reports E0223 for an ambiguous associated type and tailors suggestions based on whether the parser likely confused a primitive type with a `std` module or whether candidate types/traits are known, producing fully qualified path examples accordingly. This method does not call any other method from the provided Methods List.

Reports E0034 for multiple applicable inherent associated items, labels the ambiguous name, and then adds per-candidate notes. This method explicitly calls `note_ambiguous_inherent_assoc_ty` from the Methods List to attach those candidate notes.

Adds notes describing the candidate inherent impls for an ambiguous associated item, including local definition spans when available and truncating the list after a small limit with an `and N others` note. This method does not call any other method from the provided Methods List.

Reports that an inherent associated type was not found on a concrete self type, either listing impl types that define the item when there are no fulfillment errors or turning failed obligations into bound-oriented notes and labels when candidate impls exist but their requirements are unsatisfied. This method does not call any other method from the provided Methods List.

Diagnoses omitted associated types in trait-object or bound syntax by collecting missing associated items, reporting object-safety violations when necessary, adjusting spans for expression/pattern contexts, and constructing grouped suggestions keyed by trait name and associated type names. This method does not call any other method from the provided Methods List.

Detects a specific parser confusion where a type-relative path that looks like an associated type actually matches an inherent associated function with a combined name, and emits an E0223 diagnostic suggesting that function name instead. This method does not call any other method from the provided Methods List.

Builds and emits an error for generic arguments used where they are forbidden, classifying the argument kinds present, deriving human-readable names and spans for the affected path segments, and labeling the relevant generic argument locations. This method explicitly calls `generics_args_err_extend` from the Methods List to add context-specific notes and suggestions before emission.

Reports E0225 when a trait object contains more than one non-auto trait, labels the first and additional offending traits, suggests creating a new supertrait aliasing them, and explains auto traits. This method does not call any other method from the provided Methods List.

Emits `TraitObjectDeclaredWithNoTraits` for a trait object with no actual traits, optionally pointing at a trait alias span if one of the bounds came from a trait alias. This method does not call any other method from the provided Methods List.

Rejects associated item constraints in syntactic positions where they are not allowed, optionally shows the desugared `Fn`-trait form, and prefers either converting the constraint into a matching generic argument or removing it while also offering context-sensitive fixes for trait/impl bounds. This function explicitly calls `fn_trait_to_string` from the Methods List to render parenthesized `Fn`-trait expansions.

Formats `Fn`-family trait syntax from a path segment by reconstructing the tupled input arguments and `Output` constraint from source snippets, returning either `Fn(A) -> B` or `Fn<(A,), Output=B>` style text depending on the `parenthesized` flag. This function does not call any other method from the provided Methods List.

Extends a previously created generic-arguments error with specialized notes, labels, and rewrite suggestions for different contexts such as enum variants, primitive types, generic parameters, `Self`, and impl-associated paths. This function does not call any other method from the provided Methods List.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_ast_lowering/src/path.rs:: Lowers an AST path plus optional `QSelf` into an HIR `QPath`, using resolver `PartialRes` to split the resolved base from unresolved projections, handling async trait-bound remapping, and constructing either resolved or type-relative path forms. It calls `lower_ty` to lower the `QSelf` type, `lower_res` to convert the base resolution, `map_trait_to_async_trait` when an `async` bound targets an `Fn*` trait, `lower_path_segment` to lower every path segment with the appropriate generic-argument mode, `mark_span_with_reason` to tag desugared async-bound spans, `lower_span` for final HIR spans, and `next_id` when synthesizing type-relative HIR nodes.

Lowers an import path into `hir::UsePath`, preserving the provided per-namespace `Res` list and lowering each segment in a context where generic arguments are rejected. It calls `lower_path_segment` for each path segment and `lower_span` for the resulting path span.

Lowers one AST `PathSegment` into an HIR path segment by converting its identifier, resolution, and generic arguments, while diagnosing invalid parenthesized generics, return-type notation misuse, and missing angle brackets. It calls `lower_angle_bracketed_parameter_data` for `<...>` arguments, `lower_parenthesized_parameter_data` for `(...)` function-trait style arguments, `maybe_insert_elided_lifetimes_in_path` to synthesize omitted lifetime arguments when required, `lower_node_id`, `lower_ident`, and `lower_res` to finish the HIR segment, and uses resolver-backed `expect_full_res` to fetch the segment resolution.

Inserts synthesized elided lifetime generic arguments at the front of a path segment when the resolver recorded an elision anchor, choosing a diagnostic span based on whether brackets and other arguments are present. It calls `lower_lifetime` for each generated anonymous lifetime before wrapping them as lifetime generic arguments.

Lowers angle-bracketed generic arguments and associated-item constraints into an intermediate `GenericArgsCtor`, while also reporting whether the arguments are effectively elidable in optional-parameter mode. It calls `lower_generic_arg` for each non-constraint generic argument and `lower_assoc_item_constraint` for each associated-item constraint.

Lowers parenthesized function-trait-style generic arguments by turning inputs into a tuple argument and the return type into an `Output` associated type constraint, while enforcing the allowed `impl Trait` contexts and propagating async-bound feature tagging. It calls `lower_ty_direct` to lower input types, `lower_ty` to lower the return type under the correct `ImplTraitContext`, `ty_tup` to build tuple types for inputs or default unit output, `mark_span_with_reason` to tag desugared async-bound output spans, and `assoc_ty_binding` to create the synthetic `Output = ...` constraint.

Builds an HIR associated-type equality constraint like `Output = T` with empty generic arguments and fresh HIR identity data. It calls `next_id` to allocate the constraint HIR id and `lower_span` to lower the source span.

Maps the lang-item `Fn`, `FnMut`, or `FnOnce` trait `DefId` to its corresponding async function-trait lang item, returning `None` for all other traits. It does not call other methods from the listed methods set.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir_typeck/src/check.rs::: Type-checks a function body by preparing the `FnCtxt` state, replacing opaque return types with inference variables, forbidding invalid intrinsic ABIs, gathering locals, checking parameter patterns and well-formedness, enforcing sizedness constraints, checking the body, and reconciling the coerced body result with the declared return type; it explicitly calls `forbid_intrinsic_abi` and uses `GatherLocalsVisitor::new(...).visit_body(...)` to collect locals before parameter/body checking.

Validates that the panic handler lang item has the required non-generic function form by constructing the expected `for<'a, 'b> fn(&'a PanicInfo<'b>) -> !` signature and explicitly calling `check_function_signature` to compare it against the actual signature.

Validates the `start` lang item signature by building the expected `fn(main: fn() -> T, argc: isize, argv: *const *const u8, sigpipe: u8) -> isize` form and explicitly calling `check_function_signature` to enforce it.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir_typeck/src/coercion.r: Returns the wrapped `FnCtxt` reference so `Coerce` can transparently use `FnCtxt` APIs; it does not call any other method from the listed methods.

Checks whether coercion from one mutability to another is allowed, permitting weakening from mutable to immutable and rejecting strengthening; it does not call any other method from the listed methods.
Builds an empty adjustment list for coercions that need no HIR/MIR adjustment; it does not call any other method from the listed methods.
Creates a closure that wraps a single `Adjust` into a one-element adjustment list targeting the inferred type; it does not call any other method from the listed methods.
Packages adjustments, target type, and generated obligations into a successful `CoerceResult`; it does not call any other method from the listed methods.
Constructs a `Coerce` helper with the given `FnCtxt`, obligation cause, and two-phase-borrow policy, initializing it in subtyping mode; it does not call any other method from the listed methods.

Performs the underlying type relation for coercion, using either LUB or supertype unification under a snapshot and, with the next solver, filtering out impossible obligations before succeeding; it does not call any other method from the listed methods.
Runs `unify` and, on success, converts the unified target type into adjustments and a final coercion result by calling `unify` and `success`.

Main coercion dispatcher: resolves shallow type vars, handles `!` to any, unresolved-source fallback, unsizing, pointer/reference/dyn-star coercions, function-item/fn-pointer/closure conversions, and otherwise falls back to unification. It explicitly calls `success`, `simple`, `coerce_from_inference_variable`, `coerce_unsized`, `coerce_unsafe_ptr`, `coerce_borrowed_pointer`, `coerce_dyn_star`, `coerce_from_fn_item`, `coerce_from_fn_pointer`, `coerce_closure_to_fn`, and `unify_and`.

Handles coercion when the source is an unresolved type variable: if both sides are unresolved it emits `Coerce` obligations toward a chosen target, otherwise it falls back to subtype/LUB unification by calling `unify_and`.

Implements coercions to borrowed references, including mutability checks, fallback when the source is not already a reference, and autoderef-plus-autoref reborrows that search for a matching referent. It explicitly calls `coerce_mutbls`, `unify_and`, `unify`, and `success`.

Attempts unsizing-based coercions after rejecting unresolved types, handling reborrows for references/raw pointers, creating the necessary pointer adjustments, and proving `Unsize`/`CoerceUnsized` obligations before returning. It explicitly calls `coerce_mutbls` and `unify_and`.

Implements coercion to `dyn*`: if source and target already have the same principal trait object it falls back to plain unification, otherwise it builds existential, outlives, and `PointerLike` obligations and emits a `DynStar` adjustment. It explicitly calls `unify_and`.

Shared helper for safe-function coercions that conditionally inserts a safe-to-unsafe fn-pointer conversion, otherwise performs normal unification, then leak-checks the snapshot before committing. It explicitly calls `unify_and`.

Handles coercion from a function pointer type, chiefly allowing safe-to-unsafe weakening through the shared helper. It explicitly calls `coerce_from_safe_fn`, `simple`, and uses `identity` for the non-adjusting path.

Handles coercion from a function item by normalizing the target, rejecting intrinsic and forbidden target-feature casts, reifying the item to a fn pointer when needed, and then delegating safe/unsafe function coercion; otherwise it falls back to plain unification. It explicitly calls `coerce_from_safe_fn`, `simple`, and `unify_and`.

Coerces a non-capturing closure to a function pointer by constructing the unclosed fn-pointer signature and unifying it with a closure-fn-pointer adjustment; capturing closures or non-fn-pointer targets fall back to plain unification. It explicitly calls `unify_and`, `simple`, and uses `identity` for the fallback path.

Implements coercion to raw pointers from references or other raw pointers, checking mutability compatibility and choosing between reborrow-style raw-pointer formation, mut-to-const weakening, or no-op pointer unification. It explicitly calls `unify_and`, `coerce_mutbls`, `simple`, and uses `identity` for fallback/no-op cases.

Top-level expression coercion entry point: resolves source/target types, builds a `Coerce` helper, runs coercion in a snapshot, registers resulting obligations, applies adjustments to the expression, and returns the coerced target or an error type. It explicitly calls `Coerce::new` and `Coerce::coerce`.

Predicate-style check for whether one type can coerce to another by probing a `Coerce` run and ensuring all produced obligations can be selected. It explicitly calls `Coerce::new` and `Coerce::coerce`.
Searches autoderef steps to find the first intermediate type that can unify with the target and returns that deref count. It explicitly calls `Coerce::new` and `Coerce::unify`.
Diagnostic helper that autodereferences once and returns the dereferenced type only if the original type may implement `DerefMut`; it does not call any other method from the listed methods.

Computes a coercion-aware least upper bound across expressions, first trying ordinary LUB, then special-casing distinct function items and non-capturing closures by reifying them to compatible fn pointers and applying the resulting adjustments to prior coercion sites. It explicitly calls `Coerce::new` and `FnCtxt::coerce`.
Convenience wrapper that creates a root type-checking context and `FnCtxt`, then asks that context whether `ty` can coerce to `output_ty`. It explicitly calls `FnCtxt::can_coerce`.
Constructs a `CoerceMany` accumulator with dynamic storage for coercion sites. It explicitly calls `CoerceMany::make`.
Constructs a `CoerceMany` accumulator using a pre-supplied slice of coercion sites. It explicitly calls `CoerceMany::make`.
Internal constructor that initializes the expected type, optional merged type, expression storage, and push count for `CoerceMany`; it does not call any other method from the listed methods.
Returns the originally expected type tracked by the `CoerceMany` accumulator; it does not call any other method from the listed methods.
Returns the current merged/coerced type if one has been established, otherwise the initial expected type; it does not call any other method from the listed methods.
Adds one expression to the multi-expression coercion process by delegating to the internal coercion driver. It explicitly calls `coerce_inner`.
Forces the next coerced value to have type `()`, delegating all work to `coerce_inner` with the unit type and no expression node.

Performs the main multi-expression coercion step: resolves inference variables, propagates prior error types, chooses expected/found types for diagnostics, then either coerces the first expression with `fcx.coerce` or merges later expressions with `fcx.try_find_coercion_lub`. On success it updates the merged type, registers obligations, and records the coercion site via `as_coercion_site`; on failure it builds diagnostics, including calling `report_return_mismatched_types`, `is_return_ty_definitely_unsized`, and `suggest_boxing_tail_for_return_position_impl_trait` when applicable.

Checks whether both candidate tail-expression types satisfy the return-position `impl Trait` bounds, and if so emits diagnostics suggesting boxing. It probes compatibility by creating an obligation context and calling `register_obligations` and `select_where_possible`.

Builds a detailed diagnostic for return-position coercion failures. It starts with `fcx.err_ctxt().report_mismatched_types`, then adds targeted suggestions such as `suggest_missing_semicolon`, `suggest_mismatched_types_on_tail`, `suggest_semicolon_at_end`, `suggest_missing_return_type`, and `suggest_missing_break_or_return_expr` based on the surrounding HIR context.

Determines whether the enclosing function's return type is definitely not `Sized`. It calls `body_fn_sig` to get the function signature and `predicate_may_hold` on a constructed `Sized` obligation over `sig.output()`.
Finishes coercion accumulation by returning the computed final type if one exists, or `!` when no non-never inputs were successfully pushed.
Trait requirement that returns the HIR expression to use as the coercion site; it does not call other listed methods.
Returns the expression itself as the coercion site; it does not call other listed methods.
Forwards coercion-site lookup through a shared reference by calling `as_coercion_site` on the underlying `T`.
Unreachable implementation for the never type that returns `*self` as the coercion site; it does not call other listed methods.
Uses a match arm's body expression as the coercion site; it does not call other listed methods.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir_analysis/src/collect/: Collects and validates hidden-type constraints for an `impl Trait` used in an associated type by finding the enclosing impl, iterating its sibling associated consts/functions, and invoking `TaitConstraintLocator::check` on each possible defining item. After collection, it compares the first found hidden type against `locator.typeck_types` via `build_mismatch_error`, and emits an unconstrained-opaque error if no defining use is found.

Finds hidden-type constraints for a type-alias `impl Trait` by computing its defining HIR scope and traversing that scope with `TaitConstraintLocator`, using `walk_toplevel_module` for crate scope or explicitly calling `visit_item`, `visit_impl_item`, `visit_trait_item`, or `visit_foreign_item` on the defining node so sibling defining uses are included. It then cross-checks the chosen hidden type against collected `typeck_types` via `build_mismatch_error`, and reports an unconstrained opaque if nothing constrained it.

Per-item constraint checker for TAIT/associated opaque discovery: it skips items without typeck results, rejects `_`-inferred function returns by creating an error type, reads `typeck` results, filters `concrete_opaque_types` down to the target opaque, records typeck-visible hidden types, validates the item against `opaque_types_defined_by`, and then uses `mir_borrowck` to obtain the region-precise hidden type. When multiple defining uses disagree, it reports the mismatch with `build_mismatch_error` and updates or preserves `self.found` accordingly.
Returns the HIR map from `self.tcx.hir()` so `TaitConstraintLocator` can recursively traverse nested HIR nodes.
Visits expressions for TAIT constraint discovery; when it sees a closure, it calls `TaitConstraintLocator::check` on the closure's `def_id`, then continues traversal with `intravisit::walk_expr`.

Visits an item in the TAIT reveal scope, skipping the opaque item itself; for every other item it calls `TaitConstraintLocator::check` on the item's `def_id` and then recurses with `intravisit::walk_item`.
Visits an impl item during TAIT constraint search, skips the opaque item itself, calls `TaitConstraintLocator::check` on other impl items, and then continues with `intravisit::walk_impl_item`.
Visits a trait item for TAIT constraint collection by calling `TaitConstraintLocator::check` on the trait item's `def_id` and then recursing with `intravisit::walk_trait_item`.

Visits a foreign item only to continue traversal with `intravisit::walk_foreign_item`; it intentionally does not call `TaitConstraintLocator::check` because foreign items are not borrow-checked and cannot constrain the opaque.

Computes the hidden type for a return-position `impl Trait` by first scanning `typeck(owner_def_id).concrete_opaque_types` for the target opaque, normalizing each candidate with `remap_generic_params_to_declaration_params`, and using `build_mismatch_error` to stash HIR-level inconsistencies. It then queries `mir_borrowck(owner_def_id)` for the authoritative hidden type and, if present, traverses the owner body with `intravisit::walk_item`, `walk_impl_item`, or `walk_trait_item` using `RpitConstraintChecker` so nested bodies can be checked for mismatching constraints; otherwise it returns an error or diverging default type.

Checks one nested body for RPIT consistency by reading `mir_borrowck(def_id).concrete_opaque_types`, filtering to the target opaque, and comparing each discovered hidden type against `self.found`; on disagreement it reports the mismatch via `build_mismatch_error` and emits the diagnostic.
Returns `self.tcx.hir()` as the nested visit map so `RpitConstraintChecker` can traverse nested HIR structure.
Visits expressions while checking RPIT constraints; for closures it calls `RpitConstraintChecker::check` on the closure's `def_id`, then continues traversal with `intravisit::walk_expr`.
Visits an item in RPIT checking, skipping the opaque item itself; for every other item it calls `RpitConstraintChecker::check` on the item's `def_id` and then recurses with `intravisit::walk_item`.
Visits an impl item during RPIT checking, skips the opaque item itself, calls `RpitConstraintChecker::check` on other impl items, and continues traversal with `intravisit::walk_impl_item`.
Visits a trait item for RPIT checking by calling `RpitConstraintChecker::check` on the trait item's `def_id` and then recursing with `intravisit::walk_trait_item`.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir_analysis/src/check/wf: Returns the underlying `ObligationCtxt` by dereferencing `WfCheckingCtxt`; it does not call other methods from the Methods List.
Returns the `TyCtxt` stored in the inference context inside the obligation context; it does not call other methods from the Methods List.
Normalizes a type-foldable value under the current parameter environment, attaching a `WellFormed` obligation cause for diagnostics; it does not call other methods from the Methods List.
Builds and registers a `WellFormed` predicate obligation for a generic argument using the current body and parameter environment. It calls `WfCheckingCtxt::tcx`.

Creates the temporary inference/obligation context used for well-formedness checking, runs the supplied checker closure, solves obligations, computes implied bounds, lints redundant lifetimes, and resolves/report regions with a compatibility path for some implied-bounds cases; it does not call other methods from the Methods List.

Top-level dispatcher that selects the appropriate WF checker for the HIR node kind and then checks each generic parameter. It calls `check_item`, `check_trait_item`, `check_impl_item`, `check_foreign_item`, `check_item_type`, and `check_param_wf`.

Checks item-level well-formedness after precollecting item types, handling impls, functions, statics/consts/type aliases, ADTs, and traits according to item kind. It calls `check_impl`, `check_item_fn`, `check_item_type`, `check_type_defn`, and `check_trait`.
Checks a foreign item after precollecting its type information, validating foreign functions and statics while accepting foreign types unchanged. It calls `check_item_fn` and `check_item_type`.
